title: Add copy-on-highlight to mouse utilities
author: desi76
summary: Global copy-on-highlight would require reliable cross-application text-selection access and unconditional clipboard writes, neither of which Mouse Utilities currently owns.

status.label: Not a bounded PowerToys action
status.detail: Text selection semantics are controlled by each application or custom control, while Mouse Utilities is pointer-focused and has no universal selected-text contract; global automatic copying would also create privacy and clipboard-safety risks.

next_action.label: Post an out-of-scope explanation and direct users to application-specific copy-on-selection settings.

judgment.recommended_action: Post an out-of-scope explanation and direct users to application-specific copy-on-selection settings.

issue_context.summary: Global copy-on-highlight would require reliable cross-application text-selection access and unconditional clipboard writes, neither of which Mouse Utilities currently owns.
known_information: The reporter wants selected text copied automatically, optionally on drag or triple-click.
The requested use cases span switching between windows and completing forms.
Mouse Utilities currently observes pointer interactions but does not own application text models.
inferences: A global implementation would be unreliable for custom-rendered controls and could overwrite the clipboard when users merely select sensitive text.
issue_context.analysis: The feature cannot be bounded to a normal Mouse Utilities input gesture because the required payload is application-owned selected text. The reliability and privacy costs outweigh a generic system-wide implementation.
initial_investigation: Searched Mouse Utilities and related modules for UI Automation SelectionPattern/TextPattern support and found no existing selection-retrieval seam.
Clipboard helpers in the repository are used by utilities that explicitly own the copied content, unlike arbitrary third-party selections.

actions.label: Post scope and safety response

comment.body: Thanks for the idea. Mouse Utilities can observe pointer input, but selected text and its copy semantics are owned by each application or control; Windows does not provide one reliable, universal selected-text contract for every UI. A global copy-on-highlight feature would also overwrite the clipboard across apps, including potentially sensitive fields, and would fail on many custom controls. This is not a safe bounded Mouse Utilities feature. Application- or terminal-specific copy-on-selection settings are the reliable approach.
